briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Cannabis Industry Bets on Democratic Tax Repeal as SCOTUS Spurns Pontiac Case; DEA Moves to Boost Psychedelics Quotas Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan cannabis operators who backed Republican John James's pledge to kill the state's 24% wholesale marijuana tax say they're now "thrilled" that Democrats swept Lansing instead, with a bipartisan group of state senators already signed onto bills to repeal the levy outright. Separately, the U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear a Pontiac-based developer's bid to revive its suit against the city over delayed cannabis-business approvals, leaving a Sixth Circuit dismissal in place. Nationally, the DEA proposed sharply higher 2027 production quotas for psychedelics like psilocybin and MDMA under President Trump's April executive order on psychedelics research and access, while previewing a separate approach to marijuana quotas once full Schedule III rescheduling is finalized. Massachusetts lawmakers approved bills expanding medical marijuana access and shielding cannabis users from employment discrimination, and the National Congress of American Indians pressed the Justice Department to rewrite its marijuana rescheduling rule to explicitly cover tribally regulated cannabis.

local.text: Michigan cannabis operators who backed GOP governor candidate John James over his pledge to cut the state's 24% wholesale marijuana tax say they're now "thrilled" a Democratic trifecta took Lansing instead — a bipartisan group of state senators has signed onto bills to repeal the tax outright.

The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear Rubicon Real Estate Holdings' appeal in its fight with the city of Pontiac, leaving in place a Sixth Circuit ruling that the city's delays in approving a proposed cannabis redevelopment were bureaucratic rather than a constitutional violation.

national.text: The DEA proposed sharply higher 2027 production quotas for psychedelics like psilocybin and MDMA, citing President Trump's April executive order expanding psychedelics research and access, while previewing a separate approach to marijuana quotas once full Schedule III rescheduling is finalized.
Massachusetts lawmakers approved bills expanding the state's medical marijuana program and protecting cannabis users from employment discrimination.

The National Congress of American Indians called on the Justice Department to rewrite or supplement its marijuana rescheduling order, arguing the administration failed to consult tribes and that tribally regulated cannabis needs to be explicitly covered.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Recalls THC Gummies as Tax Portal Reopening Nears; Compass Pathways Completes Psilocybin NDA as Hemp Fights Escalate in Illinois, Texas Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan regulators and manufacturer The Gummie Joint issued a public health advisory and voluntary recall of Naked Hippie Lucky Berry gummies after consumers reported an unpleasant high and digestive distress, even as the state's marijuana retail excise-tax portal counts down to its planned Nov. 12 reopening on the new MiTreasury eServices platform following an outage that began Oct. 30. Nationally, Compass Pathways completed its COMP360 psilocybin New Drug Application to the FDA for treatment-resistant depression, targeting a first-half-2027 launch under the agency's expedited National Priority Voucher review and intensifying its race with fellow NDA-filer Usona Institute. Hemp retailers kept fighting state THC crackdowns ahead of the federal ban: an Illinois trade group sued to block the state's Nov. 12 Hemp Act ban on most hemp-derived THC products outside licensed dispensaries, while Texas's hemp industry voiced fresh optimism after the midterms installed friendlier state leadership. In cannabis business news, multistate operator Cresco Labs posted $173 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% year-over-year, with a 20.2% adjusted EBITDA margin despite a $15 million net loss.

local.text: Michigan regulators and The Gummie Joint issue a voluntary recall of Naked Hippie Lucky Berry gummies — The Cannabis Regulatory Agency's public health and safety advisory followed complaints that the 5-mg-per-piece edibles, sold in 40-count packs, caused an unpleasant high and digestive distress.

Michigan's marijuana retail excise-tax portal counts down to its planned Nov. 12 return — The system has been offline since Oct. 30 for the state's migration to the new MiTreasury eServices Business Portal, and existing account connections won't carry over when the Wholesale Marijuana Tax and retail excise-tax services both resume.

national.text: Compass Pathways completes its COMP360 psilocybin NDA submission to the FDA — The company finished filing its New Drug Application for the treatment-resistant-depression therapy, backed by two statistically significant Phase 3 trials and a Phase 2b study, and is targeting a launch in the first half of 2027 under the FDA's National Priority Voucher review track.

Illinois hemp industry sues to block the state's sweeping THC ban before it takes effect Nov. 12 — A trade group filed an emergency motion seeking to pause the new Hemp Act, which would ban most hemp-derived THC beverages and cannabinoid products from sale outside licensed dispensaries.

Texas hemp industry voices new optimism after the midterms reshape state leadership — Advocates point to incoming lawmakers seen as friendlier to THC products, even as a San Antonio councilman separately pushes to advance cannabis legalization locally.

Cresco Labs posts $173 million in Q3 revenue, up 5% year-over-year — The multistate operator reported a 20.2% adjusted EBITDA margin and converted more than 60% of adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow, even as it booked a $15 million net loss tied partly to one-time M&A and uplisting costs.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's Tax Portal Reopening Nears as Industry Eyes Lansing's Democratic Trifecta; Canopy Growth Posts Strong Earnings as Organigram-Curaleaf Fight for Aurora Continues Nationally
briefs.top: With Michigan's marijuana retail excise-tax e-services portal still offline ahead of its planned Nov. 12 return on a new platform, cannabis operators continue looking to the state's incoming Democratic trifecta for relief from the 24% wholesale tax that backers of defeated GOP nominee John James had promised to repeal, while Big Prairie Township's and Boyne Falls' post-election votes to welcome cannabis businesses add to a wave of local ballot wins. Nationally, Canopy Growth reported fiscal second-quarter net revenue growth of 22%, led by a 141% jump in international cannabis sales, as Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis continues to compete with Organigram's agreed C$561 million friendly deal and Tilray moves to consolidate Redecan production in Canada, while the DEA's rejection of a Washington, D.C. medical dispensary's federal registration bid continues to raise questions about how broadly the agency will deny Schedule III status to adult-use-state operators.

local.text: Michigan's marijuana retail excise-tax portal remains offline ahead of planned Nov. 12 return — The state took the system down Oct. 30 to migrate reporting to the new MiTreasury eServices Business Portal; the Wholesale Marijuana Tax stays unavailable through Nov. 11, and existing account connections won't carry over when both systems resume Nov. 12.

Big Prairie Township and Boyne Falls add to Michigan's post-election wave of cannabis-friendly votes — Big Prairie Township voters approved a state-licensed adult-use consumption lounge, while Boyne Falls voters rejected a ban on marijuana establishments, joining Bad Axe, Menominee and Mottville Township in loosening local restrictions after the Nov. 3 election.

Michigan cannabis operators still hope a Democratic trifecta brings 24% wholesale-tax relief — Operators who backed Republican John James for his pledge to repeal the tax are now looking to Lansing's new Democratic-controlled government for relief, as the state's shrinking cannabis market continues to feel the tax's impact.

national.text: Canopy Growth posts 22% net revenue growth in fiscal Q2, led by international cannabis surge — The Canadian producer's net revenue growth was driven by a 141% increase in international markets cannabis sales for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, the company reported Nov. 6.

Organigram-Aurora deal and Curaleaf's rival bid headline a busy week in Canadian cannabis business — Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis remains outstanding even after Aurora's board backed Organigram's friendly acquisition, while Tilray announced it will close its Fenwick, Ontario facility and shift Redecan production to other sites.

DEA rejects a Washington, D.C. dispensary's federal registration bid — The agency's Order to Show Cause said it can't register any dispensary under D.C.'s program because the district allows dispensing without a written medical certification, raising concern the DEA may deny Schedule III registration broadly to adult-use-state operators.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Marijuana Tax Portal Set to Reopen Nov. 12 as Big Prairie Township, Boyne Falls Join Post-Election Cannabis Wave; Democrats' Midterm Wins Fuel Federal Reform Hopes Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan marijuana retailers are bracing for the Nov. 12 reopening of the state's MiTreasury eServices tax portal after a planned two-week migration outage, even as Big Prairie Township and Boyne Falls became the latest Michigan communities to embrace cannabis businesses in the wake of the Nov. 3 election, joining Bad Axe, Menominee and Mottville Township. Nationally, Democrats' retaking of the House and Senate majorities has advocates and even a former Trump adviser touting new bipartisan momentum for federal cannabis reform, Marijuana Moment's newsletters report, while the DEA rejected a Washington, D.C. medical dispensary's federal registration bid over the district's lack of a written-certification requirement — a sign the agency may deny Schedule III status broadly to adult-use-state operators. Missouri's attorney general sued four retailers for allegedly selling marijuana as hemp and beat back a court challenge to the state's intoxicating-cannabinoid law, and Aurora Cannabis posted record C$61.4 million in international medical revenue in its fiscal Q2.

local.text: Michigan's marijuana retail excise-tax system set to reopen Nov. 12 — The MiTreasury eServices portal has been offline since Oct. 30 for a planned migration, with the marijuana tax call center closed Nov. 4-6; existing account connections won't carry over, though MiLogin for Business credentials still work.

Big Prairie Township and Boyne Falls join Michigan's post-election wave of cannabis-friendly votes — Big Prairie Township voters approved allowing one state-licensed adult-use consumption lounge, while Boyne Falls voters rejected an ordinance banning marijuana establishments, adding to Nov. 3 results that also saw Bad Axe and Menominee lift restrictions and Mottville Township keep its two dispensaries open.

national.text: Lawmakers and strategists see bipartisan opening for federal cannabis reform — Rep. Dina Titus (D-NV) and longtime Trump adviser Roger Stone both told Marijuana Moment the midterm results could create new momentum for reform, as top Wisconsin lawmakers said the state is positioned to legalize marijuana under incoming Democratic control.

Democrats' midterm wins raise hopes for federal marijuana reform — With Democrats retaking House and Senate majorities, Congressional Cannabis Caucus co-chair Dina Titus pledged to keep pushing for banking access and rescheduling, and the National Cannabis Industry Association's board chair called it a new opening for comprehensive federal reform.

DEA rejects a Washington, D.C. dispensary's federal registration bid — The agency's Order to Show Cause said it can't register any dispensary under D.C.'s program because the district allows dispensing without a written medical certification, echoing a similar denial to a Minneapolis dual-use retailer and raising concern the DEA may deny Schedule III registration broadly to adult-use-state operators.

Missouri AG sues four retailers over alleged marijuana-as-hemp sales — Attorney General Catherine Hanaway's office accused Puffers Choice, CBD Kratom Cannabis Dispensary, Herb Depot and Token THC Dispensary of selling products that tested above hemp's THC limit while posing as licensed dispensaries, and a federal court the same day dismissed a challenge to the state's intoxicating-cannabinoid law.

Aurora Cannabis posts record international medical revenue in fiscal Q2 — Net revenue rose 9% to C$86.0 million, driven by record international medical cannabis revenue of C$61.4 million (up 44%) on higher demand in Germany and Poland, even as adjusted EBITDA slipped to C$14.0 million from C$15.4 million a year earlier.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Cannabis Industry Eyes Dem Trifecta for Tax Relief as Bad Axe Ends Pot Ban; Idaho Rejects Drug-Ballot Power Grab as Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates Nationally
briefs.top: Fresh off Tuesday's election, Michigan cannabis operators who largely backed Republican John James over his pledge to cut the 24% wholesale tax are now looking to the state's new Democratic trifecta for relief, even as Crain's Detroit Business warns the industry's core problems — the tax, falling prices and oversupply — need a legislative fix regardless of who's in charge; separately, Huron County's Bad Axe ended a seven-year local ban on marijuana businesses. Nationally, Idaho voters crushed a legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would have stripped citizens of the right to put marijuana and other drug policy on the ballot, rejecting it roughly two-to-one, while cannabis earnings season rolled on: Curaleaf posted record $353 million in Q3 revenue, Green Thumb Industries grew revenue 11.3% to $324.4 million, and Trulieve beat Wall Street estimates with $230 million despite a year-over-year decline.

local.text: Michigan cannabis operators hope Democratic trifecta brings tax relief — Operators who backed Republican John James for his pledge to cut the 24% wholesale tax are now looking to Lansing's new Democratic-controlled government for relief, even as the state's $3.17 billion cannabis market keeps shrinking.

Crain's: Democratic control raises stakes for Michigan's 'floundering' weed companies — With Democrats holding the governor's office and both legislative chambers for only the second time since 1982, the piece argues the industry's core problems — the 24% wholesale tax, falling prices and oversupply — still need a legislative fix regardless of which party is in charge.

Bad Axe voters end seven-year ban on marijuana businesses — The Huron County city's Nov. 3 ballot measure overturned a longstanding prohibition on cannabis establishments, part of the same election that also raised Menominee's dispensary cap from nine to 13.

national.text: Idaho voters crush HJR 4, preserving citizens' right to put drug policy on the ballot — About two-thirds of voters rejected the legislatively referred amendment that would have stripped Idahoans of the ability to use citizen initiatives to legalize marijuana, narcotics or other psychoactive substances.

Curaleaf posts record $353 million in Q3 revenue, beating estimates — The multistate operator's third-quarter net revenue rose 11% year-over-year, with international sales up 28%, and adjusted EBITDA reached $78 million on a 49% adjusted gross margin.

Green Thumb Industries posts $324.4 million in Q3 revenue, up 11.3% — The Chicago-based operator added six Rise dispensaries across three states during the quarter and reported normalized EBITDA of $89.4 million, or 27.6% of revenue.

Trulieve beats Q3 estimates with $230 million in revenue despite year-over-year decline — The Florida-based operator topped Wall Street's roughly $221.7 million consensus with a 64% gross margin and $89 million in adjusted EBITDA, and guided to low-single-digit revenue growth in Q4.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Benson Beats James as Niles, Mottville and Menominee Settle Dispensary Fights; Massachusetts and Houston Deliver Cannabis Wins Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's Nov. 3 election reshaped the state's cannabis landscape: Democrat Jocelyn Benson defeated Republican John James — who had the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's backing for his pledge to repeal the 24% wholesale tax — in the governor's race, while voters in three border communities split on dispensary rules: Niles capped retailers at five and its township kept a ban on expansion, Mottville Township voters rejected shutting down its two existing shops, and Menominee raised its licensing cap from nine to 13. Nationally, cannabis had a banner election night as Massachusetts voters crushed a repeal of recreational sales roughly 76%-24% and Houston approved deprioritizing marijuana enforcement, while in the business world Organigram topped Curaleaf's hostile bid to acquire Aurora Cannabis and Usona Institute filed its psilocybin NDA with the FDA.

local.text: Niles voters cap marijuana retailers citywide while neighboring township keeps its ban — City of Niles voters approved limiting marijuana retailers to five and microbusinesses to four, 61%-39%, while Niles Charter Township voters narrowly rejected, 52%-48%, a measure that would have allowed up to four recreational retailers there.

Mottville Township voters reject ban on its two dispensaries — A proposed ordinance that would have shut down the border township's only two marijuana retailers failed at the polls, 379 votes against to 215 in favor, so both shops continue operating.

Menominee voters raise dispensary cap from nine to 13 — City voters approved a referendum expanding the number of marijuana retail licenses allowed in Menominee, 1,812 to 1,212, clearing the way for up to four more shops in the Wisconsin-border city.

Jocelyn Benson defeats John James for governor, clouding the 24% wholesale tax's future — Democrat Benson won the race to succeed term-limited Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, beating Republican John James, who had the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's backing for his pledge to repeal or sharply cut the state's 24% wholesale marijuana tax; Benson has called the tax a 'new and emerging issue' and her running mate voted for it.

national.text: Massachusetts voters crush Question 8, keeping recreational marijuana legal — Roughly 76% of voters rejected the SAM Action-backed measure that would have repealed the state's adult-use cannabis law and ended licensed retail sales by 2028, a decade after Massachusetts first legalized.

Houston voters approve Proposition A, deprioritizing marijuana enforcement — The charter amendment makes low-level marijuana possession the Houston Police Department's lowest enforcement priority and bans no-knock warrants; it doesn't legalize cannabis, which remains illegal under Texas law.

Federal hemp-THC ban deadline slips to Dec. 11, but synthetic cannabinoid ban still hits Nov. 12 — A bipartisan Senate push delayed the new total-THC standard and per-container potency cap by a month via H.R. 6500, which Trump signed Sept. 2, but the ban on synthetic cannabinoids in hemp products remains on track for Nov. 12.

Organigram tops Curaleaf's hostile bid, agrees to buy Aurora Cannabis — Organigram will acquire all of Aurora's outstanding shares for C$7.80 apiece, valuing the Canadian producer at roughly C$561 million; both boards approved the friendly deal, which offers a 21% premium over Curaleaf's competing offer, and Curaleaf says its hostile bid remains active.

Usona Institute files psilocybin NDA with FDA for major depressive disorder — The nonprofit psychedelics research group completed its new drug application for psilocybin as a treatment for major depressive disorder, intensifying its race with Compass Pathways, which is finishing its own rolling NDA for COMP360 this quarter.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: DEA Rebuffs Bid to Reopen Rescheduling Hearing as Curaleaf-Aurora Fight Drags On; Michigan's Ballot Guide Previews Nov. 3 Stakes for Weed
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis industry is bracing for a Nov. 3 election that could reshape dispensary caps and the governor's race fight over the 24% wholesale tax: a new voter guide lays out the stakes, Niles voters will decide whether to cap the city at five marijuana retailers, and NORML is urging the Sixth Circuit to reconsider a ruling that voided a $31.8 million verdict for Michigan grower Hello Farms against Curaleaf subsidiaries. Nationally, the DEA told its administrative law judge it won't support rescheduling opponents' bid to reopen the hearing for new testimony, Curaleaf is pressing its hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis after Aurora's board urged shareholders to reject it again, a new UMass Amherst/WCVB poll found Massachusetts' marijuana-repeal measure trailing 61%-31%, and the Massachusetts House advanced a bill letting veterans get medical marijuana without a doctor's recommendation.

local.text: Michigan stoner's guide to voting in 2026 — With early voting opening Oct. 24, a new voter guide walks through how the governor's race, all 148 Legislature seats and a wave of local ballot questions on dispensary caps and bans could reshape the state's cannabis market.

Niles ballot measure would cap the city at five marijuana retailers — A citizen-petitioned amendment on the Nov. 3 ballot would limit the city to five provisioning centers, the number already licensed, after a resident-led group gathered enough signatures to force the vote.

NORML urges Sixth Circuit to reconsider ruling against Michigan grower Hello Farms — NORML's legal committee, led by Detroit attorney William Swor, filed a brief backing Hello Farms' bid for a rehearing after a panel voided its $31.8 million verdict against Curaleaf subsidiaries, ruling federal courts can't enforce cannabis contracts.

national.text: DEA opposes rescheduling opponents' bid to reopen hearing — The DEA told its chief administrative law judge it won't support prohibitionist groups' request for new testimony and document discovery in the marijuana rescheduling case, even as it doesn't object to adding a GAO report critical of the scheduling process to the record.

Curaleaf presses hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis as board urges shareholders to reject it again — Aurora's special committee says it's weighing other strategic alternatives, reportedly including interest from Canadian producer Organigram, after rebuffing Curaleaf's sweetened $5-per-share offer for a second time.

New poll shows Massachusetts cannabis-repeal measure trailing badly — A UMass Amherst/WCVB poll of 800 registered voters found 61% opposed to Question 8's repeal of retail marijuana sales and just 31% in favor, with Question 8 polling as the least popular of the nine ballot questions surveyed.

Massachusetts House advances bill letting veterans get medical marijuana without a doctor's recommendation — The chamber gave second-reading approval to Gov. Maura Healey's proposal, which would also add PTSD, opioid use disorder and chronic pain as qualifying conditions; it still needs a third reading and Senate passage.

Two Utica firefighters sue over medical marijuana discipline — In an op-ed, one of two New York firefighters suspended after testing positive for cannabis metabolites argues both were certified medical patients never accused of being impaired on duty, and describes their suit against the city and department.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Massachusetts Voters Crush Question 8 Repeal as Curaleaf-Aurora Feud Escalates; Delaware's THC Drink Law Kicks In
briefs.top: Massachusetts' push to repeal legal marijuana sales is cratering at the ballot box: a new Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll found voters opposing the Question 8 repeal by a 71%-21% margin, and the Globe's own editorial board joined the "No" campaign, while a new Marijuana Moment/NuggMD quarterly poll found cannabis consumers souring further on the Trump administration as federal rescheduling remains stalled. In the business world, Curaleaf is publicly sparring with Aurora Cannabis's board after it unilaterally rejected Curaleaf's sweetened hostile-takeover bid, and Delaware's new hemp-THC beverage law takes effect today, letting liquor stores and dispensaries sell THC drinks ahead of the looming federal hemp deadline. Michigan's cannabis headlines this week are still dominated by the NFL rescinding Lions receiver Jameson Williams's celebration fine, six Detroit-area defendants charged in an armed, 200-pound cannabis heist in Warren, and two Upper Peninsula operators ditching the state's 24% wholesale tax for lower-tax Minnesota.

local.text: NFL rescinds fine against Lions WR Jameson Williams — The league reversed a fine over a touchdown celebration in which Williams mimed smoking, after his camp noted cannabis is legal in both Michigan and New York.

Six Detroit-area residents charged with armed robbery in Warren — Police say the group arrived at a commercial cannabis facility on Lorna Avenue in a U-Haul and Camaro, held a security guard at gunpoint and tried to drive off with more than 200 pounds of weed; each defendant was arraigned on a $500,000 bond and must wear a GPS tether if released.

Two Upper Peninsula operators quit Michigan for lower-tax Minnesota — A pair of U.P. cannabis businessmen left the state's industry to open a new dispensary, Dankz, in St. Cloud, Minnesota, citing Michigan's steeper tax burden under the 24% wholesale tax.

national.text: Poll: Massachusetts voters crush Question 8 repeal effort — A Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll of 500 likely voters found 71.4% opposed to the November ballot measure that would repeal legal recreational marijuana sales, versus just 21.4% in support.

Boston Globe editorial board urges 'No' vote on Question 8 — The board cited more than $10 billion in legal marijuana sales since legalization and warned that repeal could push Massachusetts consumers to buy across state lines.

Poll: cannabis consumers' support for Trump administration drops further as rescheduling stalls — The latest Marijuana Moment/NuggMD quarterly tracking poll found consumer approval of the administration's handling of marijuana policy has fallen sharply as the federal rescheduling process remains stalled.

Curaleaf challenges Aurora's rejection of its enhanced buyout bid — Curaleaf publicly criticized Aurora Cannabis's board for unilaterally rejecting its sweetened offer, which it says represents a 217% premium on an ex-cash basis; Aurora's board has unanimously urged shareholders not to tender their shares.

Delaware's hemp-THC beverage law takes effect today — House Bill 373 allows THC drinks to be sold to adults 21+ at licensed liquor stores and marijuana dispensaries, with potency caps by container size and tax provisions following in February 2027.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: NFL Clears Lions Star Over Pot Celebration as Michigan Cannabis Hits the Blotter; Veterans Poll and Mass. Ballot Fight Lead National News
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis news this cycle skewed toward law-and-order: the NFL rescinded a fine against Lions receiver Jameson Williams for miming a smoke during a touchdown celebration after his camp noted the drug is legal in Michigan, while prosecutors charged six Detroit-area residents with armed robbery over an alleged 200-pound weed heist in Warren and an Illinois man was hit with a felony in Indiana over cannabis bought at a New Buffalo dispensary. Nationally, a new Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America survey found 61% of military veterans back federal legalization, Massachusetts lawmakers kept up their campaign against the Question 8 repeal measure on next month's ballot, Houston opened early voting on a measure to deprioritize marijuana enforcement, and hemp beverage makers urged customers to lobby Congress against the looming THC ban.

local.text: NFL rescinds fine against Lions WR Jameson Williams — The league reversed a fine over a touchdown celebration in which Williams mimed smoking, after his camp noted cannabis is legal in both Michigan and New York.

Illinois man charged with felony in Indiana over Michigan-bought weed — A traffic stop turned up more than an ounce of cannabis and a bag from a New Buffalo dispensary, leading to a felony charge despite the purchase being legal just across the Michigan border.

Six Detroit-area residents charged with armed robbery in Warren — Prosecutors allege the group tried to drive off with more than 200 pounds of cannabis from a Warren cannabis facility; each defendant faces a $500,000 bond.

Two Upper Peninsula operators quit Michigan for lower-tax Minnesota — A pair of U.P. cannabis businessmen left the state's industry to open a new dispensary in St. Cloud, Minnesota, citing Michigan's steeper tax burden.

national.text: Veterans poll shows majority back federal legalization — A new Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America survey found 61% of military veterans support legalizing recreational marijuana.

Hemp beverage makers rally customers to lobby Congress — With federal restrictions on hemp-derived THC drinks approaching, a hemp company is letting customers send cannabis beverages directly to their members of Congress to press for a fix.

Massachusetts lawmakers keep up fight against Question 8 — More than 60 state legislators, including the House Speaker and Senate President, are publicly urging voters to reject the November ballot measure that would repeal the state's adult-use marijuana law.

Houston opens early voting on marijuana deprioritization measure — Early voting began Oct. 19 on Proposition A, which would make low-level marijuana enforcement the Houston Police Department's lowest priority and ban no-knock warrants.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Industry Doubles Down on James as Tax Fight Drags On; DEA Stands Firm on Rescheduling Science
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis trade group formally endorsed GOP governor nominee John James over his pledge to gut the 24% wholesale tax and crack down on unregulated hemp, while a Democratic state senator warned the industry not to trust him — and hemp-reform bills remain stuck in the GOP-led House even as a Macomb County operator faces discipline over illegal hemp-derived THC concentrate. Nationally, the DEA told its administrative law judge a new GAO report has "no bearing" on the scientific case for marijuana rescheduling and is pushing back against further delay, while the psychedelics pipeline keeps moving with FDA-fast-tracked psilocybin and MDMA-like therapies from Compass Pathways, Usona and Transcend Therapeutics.

local.text: Michigan Cannabis Industry Association endorses John James for governor — The trade group backed the GOP nominee and put money behind his campaign, citing his pledge to repeal or sharply roll back the 24% wholesale marijuana tax that funds road repairs.

James's cannabis platform also targets unregulated hemp sales — Beyond the tax repeal, the Republican nominee says Delta-8, THCA and synthetic cannabinoids should face the same age limits, testing and labeling rules as licensed cannabis instead of selling freely at gas stations and smoke shops.

Democratic senator: don't trust James's tax-cut pledge — A Michigan Democratic state senator argued the GOP nominee's record of opposing cannabis reform means the industry shouldn't count on him to follow through on cutting the wholesale tax.

Hemp and license-cap bills still stuck in the GOP-led House — Packages setting up a regulatory framework for consumable hemp products and capping retail/wholesale licenses at one per 10,000 residents cleared the Democratic-controlled Senate last year but remain unresolved in the House.

Macomb County operator accused of illegal hemp-derived THC concentrate — Regulators say Harrison Township's Pure Roots/Forte Cannabis bought THCA isolate from a hemp-licensed supplier and sold concentrate that independently tested as high as 87% THC, far above the 0.3% hemp threshold, with thousands of units reaching licensed dispensaries.

national.text: DEA tells judge GAO report has 'no bearing' on rescheduling science — Responding ahead of an Oct. 13 deadline, the DEA said a new Government Accountability Office report on scheduling procedures doesn't undercut the case for moving marijuana to Schedule III, and it opposed further briefing that would delay the administrative law judge's recommendation.

Rescheduling case stays paused while judge weighs GAO motion — The DEA's chief administrative law judge has not yet ruled on admitting the GAO report or allowing more briefing, extending a stay that began Sept. 29 and pushing any recommendation on Schedule III further into the fourth quarter.

FDA fast-tracks psilocybin and MDMA-like PTSD therapies — Compass Pathways (psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression), Usona Institute (psilocybin for major depressive disorder) and Transcend Therapeutics (methylone for PTSD) each hold National Priority Vouchers that can shrink FDA review to one to two months, following an April 2026 executive order directing agencies to speed psychedelic approvals.

Compass Pathways eyes Q4 rolling NDA submission for COMP360 — After positive Phase 3 results, CEO Kabir Nath said the company is finishing a rolling New Drug Application this quarter, with a deliberately cautious rollout planned once approved.

Federal hemp THC deadline keeps states scrambling — With a late-2025 funding-deal provision putting most hemp-derived THC products on a roughly one-year federal clock, states are moving on their own: Ohio lawmakers reached a deal to ban most intoxicating hemp products including THC drinks, while Texas's push to restrict hemp-derived products keeps drawing industry pushback.

briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Demand Holds, Deals Heat Up: MI Weed Finds Its Footing as Rescheduling Fight Grinds On
briefs.top: Michigan operators are leaning into growth — a Detroit-born flower brand just cracked 90 stores and House of Dank keeps opening doors — even as the 24% wholesale tax squeezes margins and fuels a governor's-race promise to roll it back. Nationally, cannabis M&A is accelerating (Cronos just closed a European buy) and Compass Pathways says its psilocybin therapy is on track for an early-2027 launch, even as the DEA rescheduling case stays technically paused, not dead.

local.text: Detroit's Zasso scales to 90 Michigan stores — A small Detroit cultivation outfit selling top-shelf flower for about $100 an ounce hit shelves about a year ago and is now stocked in roughly 90 stores statewide, with most retailers reaching out first.
House of Dank opens new Berkley storefront — Michigan's leading cannabis retailer kept its statewide expansion rolling with a new Woodward-corridor location in Berkley.

Demand stays near all-time highs despite the tax — Consumer demand for regulated cannabis remains near a record even as low prices and the new wholesale tax push more operators toward consolidation, with dispensaries still on pace to sell over 1.3 million pounds of flower this year.

GOP governor nominee vows to gut the 24% tax — John James has pledged to repeal or sharply cut the wholesale tax, calling it a driver of higher prices and a boost to illegal operators, and industry executives have backed his campaign with real money this cycle.

Lansing lawmakers push bipartisan repeal bills — Legislators in both chambers have introduced bills to kill the controversial 24% wholesale tax as sales dip and businesses close, giving operators a legislative path forward alongside the pending court appeal.

national.text: Cronos closes European cannabis buy today — Cronos Group completed its acquisition of CanAdelaar, the largest adult-use cannabis company in the Netherlands' pilot program, establishing the top market share in Europe's largest legal cannabis market.

Compass Pathways says psilocybin launch still on for early 2027 — CEO Kabir Nath said the company is finishing its rolling FDA submission for COMP360 this quarter and plans a deliberately cautious rollout once approved.

Cannabis M&A wave keeps building post-rescheduling push — Operators like Colorado's Spherex are closing new acquisitions and investing early in integration planning as deal activity accelerates across the industry.
DEA rescheduling case paused, not dead — A DEA judge ordered the agency to respond to opponents' bid to reopen testimony, with the case formally stayed while the tribunal weighs the pending motions.

Federally funded study backs cannabis as an opioid-sparing tool — New research shows medical marijuana improves cancer-related symptoms and helps reduce opioid use, adding fresh clinical ammunition for reform advocates.
